lhd-8.tx:
The USS Theodore Roosevelt (CVN-71) carrier strike group and the USS Makin Island (LHD-8) amphibious ready group, with the embarked 13th Marine Expeditionary Unit (MEU), are headed to the Middle East, two U.S. officials told Fox News. The ships are expected to arrive by the end of November, adding about 10,000 sailors and Marines to the region. Fox reports about 6,000 are in the carrier strike group and about 4,200 in the MEU and Makin Island group, a typical size for such a force.

The Roosevelt would be the third aircraft carrier in the Middle East, joining the USS George H.W. Bush (CVN-77) and USS George Washington (CVN-73). Makin Island would be the second amphibious assault ship with an embarked MEU in the region, alongside USS Boxer (LHD-4) and the 11th MEU. The deployment comes as President Trump has said renewed military action against Iran remains possible after the November 3 midterm elections.

With a flight deck packed with carrier-based aircraft, including stealthy fifth-generation F-35Cs, the USS Theodore Roosevelt pulled into Yokosuka, Japan, on Friday. Roosevelt is the first non-resident U.S. carrier to visit the key naval port, strategically located on the east side of Japan, in more than four years. Yokosuka is home to thee USS George Washington and America’s only forward-based Carrier Strike Group (CSG).

Roosevelt, which serves as the flagship of CSG 9, escorted by guided-missile cruiser USS Chosin and destroyer USS Decatur, completed the journey from San Diego in 19 days − maneuvering around a typhoon in the Western Pacific − and will participate in the upcoming combined exercise Keen Sword 27.

The ships will arrive in the Middle East by the end of November, the officials said. These new deployments will add about 10,000 Sailors and Marines to the Middle East.

The USS Roosevelt will be the third aircraft carrier in the Middle East, joining the USS George H.W. The USS Roosevelt departed its home port of San Diego on Sunday and the 13th Marine Expeditionary Unit deployed from San Diego on Monday along with the Makin Island Amphibious Ready Group. Makin Island would be the second amphibious assault ship with an embarked MEU in the region, alongside USS Boxer (LHD-4) and the 11th MEU. The deployment comes as President Trump has said renewed military action against Iran remains possible after the November 3 midterm elections.

lhd-4.tx:
If you want to understand what it means to be an American citizen, look at what happened in the Indian Ocean on Easter Sunday, April 12, 2009.

One merchant captain from Vermont named Richard Phillips was being held hostage inside a covered orange lifeboat by Somali pirates armed with AK-47s.

He was not a general. He was not a politician. He was one cargo ship captain who had offered himself as a hostage to save his crew.

To bring that one man home, the United States sent the guided-missile destroyer USS Bainbridge, the frigate USS Halyburton, the amphibious assault ship USS Boxer, and a team of U.S. Navy SEALs who parachuted straight into the black ocean at night.

For four days, the lifeboat pitched violently in rough seas twenty-five yards behind the destroyer.

Then at dusk on Sunday, a pirate pressed the barrel of his AK-47 directly against Captain Phillips' back and prepared to kill him.

On the fantail of the USS Bainbridge, three Navy SEAL snipers lay braced in the dark. The destroyer was rolling in one direction. The tiny lifeboat was pitching in another. If even one sniper missed by half an inch, or fired a tenth of a second late, the hostage would die.

Through night-vision scopes, all three snipers waited for the exact millisecond when three targets appeared in the tiny windows at once.

One word came over the headset.

Three rifles fired as a single sound.

All three kidnappers dropped instantly. Captain Phillips walked onto the deck of the USS Bainbridge without a scratch.

Do not touch a citizen of a country that will drop Navy SEALs from the sky at midnight for one man.

cvn-76.t: If anyone ever tells you the United States military is only a machine of war, take them to the coast of Tohoku, Japan, and tell them what happened in March 201…
cvn-76.tx:
If anyone ever tells you the United States military is only a machine of war, take them to the coast of Tohoku, Japan, and tell them what happened in March 2011.

When the 9.0 earthquake and 40-foot tsunami wiped out entire towns and crippled the Fukushima nuclear plant, foreign embassies told their citizens to flee Japan immediately.

The USS Ronald Reagan Carrier Strike Group did the exact opposite.
They steamed at flank speed straight TOWARD the disaster zone.

When the first Navy helicopters touched down in the snow along the northern coast, nineteen-year-old American sailors saw something they will never forget:

Thousands of Japanese mothers, grandmothers, and small children huddled in freezing dark shelters. Their shoes had been ripped off by the black water. Their coats were soaked in icy mud.

Official relief cargo planes were still days away.
The sailors of the USS Ronald Reagan, USS Chancellorsville, and USS Preble didn't wait for orders from Washington.

They walked back to their own narrow bunks below deck and opened their personal lockers.

In just a few hours, young American sailors stripped off their own warm clothes to send ashore on the next helicopter.
The official Navy log still records what they gave from their own sea bags that afternoon:

• 748 pairs of their own socks
• 311 jackets and sweaters
• 450 shirts and 237 pairs of pants
• 57 pairs of their own shoes
• Over 100 blankets right off their racks

And here is the detail that makes grown men in Japan weep to this day:

Included in those boxes were 20 stuffed animals.
Tough nineteen-year-old sailors took the lucky teddy bears and plush toys their moms and little sisters had tucked into their sea bags back home in America—and sent them to crying Japanese children so they wouldn't be scared in the dark.

Days later, as Navy helicopters flew low over the ruined coast, pilots looked down through tears at a muddy schoolyard.
Japanese children had gathered broken white debris to spell one giant word on the ground for the American sky:

“ARIGATO.” (Thank you.)

Fifty thousand Americans came to save us in Operation Tomodachi.
In Japanese, “Tomodachi” means friend.
In our hearts, it means brother. Forever. 🇺🇸🤝🇯🇵

cvn-76.tx:
The US Navy controlled an MQ-25A Stingray refueling drone from an aircraft carrier more than 2,100 miles away. 

Operators aboard the USS Ronald Reagan in the Pacific linked to the aircraft, which was sitting at Boeing's facility in Mascoutah, Illinois.

Using the carrier's Unmanned Air Warfare Center and a low Earth orbit satellite network, the crew made a beyond-line-of-sight connection during sea trials. 

The Navy calls it the first successful link between an underway carrier's control station and an MQ-25A, a key test of the systems needed to bring drones onto future carrier decks.

A UAE government delegation has reportedly arrived in Tehran aboard a RoyalJet Boeing 737 VIP aircraft, raising questions about diplomatic efforts between the two countries. The visit comes amid claims by Iranian state media that the Trump administration sought permission for a symbolic strike on Iran’s Pickaxe Mountain site in exchange for Tehran not retaliating.

The bigger question involves Iran’s frozen funds. Reuters reported in June that the UAE had agreed to release around $10 billion in frozen Iranian assets. Other reports have claimed that earlier flights carried approximately two tonnes of gold to Tehran, but those claims have not been independently verified. Reports of additional funds being released remain unconfirmed as well.

The discussions may also be linked to regional security. Some reports suggest the UAE wants assurances that Iran would not target American military assets on Emirati soil if Washington strikes Pickaxe Mountain, particularly Al Dhafra Air Base near Abu Dhabi. However, no confirmed agreement or new financial transfer has been established, leaving the purpose and outcome of the reported visit uncertain.

muwaffaq-salti.tx:
🚨🇺🇸🇮🇷 Troops and military families leak photos of burned aircraft, bombed barracks and self-dug foxholes from the Iran war, and say the Pentagon threatened them for sharing any of it

The images come through MeidasTouch and VALOR Media from anonymous service members, contractors and spouses.

What they describe, base by base:

-Prince Sultan, Saudi Arabia: dining halls, workspaces and dorms destroyed; an AWACS and two KC-135 tankers damaged in one strike that reportedly injured 10 to 12; bunkers delivered with no doors; a photo sources say is a destroyed C-17 that the Pentagon has never acknowledged

-Muwaffaq Salti, Jordan: three months of incoming so frequent the alarms couldn't keep up; F-15s, F-35s and Reapers damaged; a ballistic missile got past interceptors and hit barracks on July 17, killing three, with troops saying they heard the wounded calling from inside the flames; housing hit twice; troops told they were going home, then ordered to stay after throwing out their bedding

-Camp Buehring, Kuwait: some troops lived out of a van in the desert for three months; September photos show the camp nearly abandoned

-UAE: no warning the war was starting, no shelters, only security teams armed; troops hid in hotels ordering takeout or dug their own foxholes; leadership described as "rudderless"

-Bahrain: Fifth Fleet headquarters damaged; families say evacuation planes were waiting but the Pentagon refused because it would "look bad at home," then the airport was hit; some paid tens of thousands to escape, hid in a mall parking garage, or were housed in residential buildings that were struck within hours; senior leaders reportedly flown out under cover of a "training exercise"

-Across the force: no embedded press, rumors of year-plus extensions, troops saying they learned the war began from the news and don't know what they're fighting for

The Pentagon’s latest number to Congress is $43.6 billion for the war, $45.1 billion with fuel, and base damage still isn’t in it. 

The people who lived in those bases just filled in the blank, and the strike plan for November expects them to do it again.

Source: @MeidasTouch / Writer: Daniel

incirlik.tx:
Trump openly lies that Zelenskyy “doesn’t care” about ending the war. He also lies that Russia is generously sending cheap diesel to the world. Russia is selling it under a deal Trump struck with Putin, after the US lifted sanctions to allow it.

Russia invaded Ukraine. Russia can stop the war any day by withdrawing. Ukraine can’t. 

Breakdown of Trump lies⬇️

“I am in the process of negotiating Peace in the war between Russia and Ukraine, and don’t want to do anything that will drive, foolishly, Russia away from the bargaining table.”

Trump lied.

Trump’s own words give other reasons for going easy on Russia. Later in the same post he says that perhaps more importantly, Russia is doing very little to help Iran and he wants to keep it that way. Bloomberg reported that he waived the Russia energy tariffs because they were getting in the way of lowering diesel prices before the midterms. When he announced the diesel deal with Putin, he didn’t mention the war or sanctions and performatively called lower prices for farmers, ranchers and truckers his greatest priority, all the meanwhile being the culprit behind the increased prices.

He has shown no similar concern about driving Ukraine away. He said Kyiv "had better damn well stop" its refinery strikes and that Ukraine should replace its president, and Ukrainian officials say US counterparts warned that the US would cut off intelligence if the strikes continued. Russia, meanwhile, hit power plants in Ukraine within hours of Trump announcing his energy ceasefire.

"Russia is doing very little, if anything, to help the Islamic Republic of Iran.”

Trump lied.

“Very little compared to what they could be doing” is a standard nobody can test. Moscow and Tehran have a deep military relationship. Russia’s air war on Ukrainian cities was built on Iranian-designed Shahed drones.

Read the sentence in context. Trump says he wants to keep Russia’s help to Iran limited and will, unless stupid people get in the way. That’s an admission that he’s going easy on Moscow over Ukraine to keep it quiet on Iran.

His own military has said otherwise. Gen. Dan Caine, chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, confirmed Russia has been aiding Iran during the war, including expanded intelligence sharing and satellite imagery to help Tehran target US forces. Ukraine has said Russian satellites photographed Diego Garcia, Incirlik in Turkey, Al Udeid in Qatar and Saudi oil and gas fields, all of which Iran later attacked.

Russia was shipping TNT, ammunition and drone components to Iran across the Caspian Sea, helping it rebuild arsenals used up fighting the US and Israel. Moscow has also coached Tehran on drone use and electronic warfare, drawing on its experience in Ukraine. Eighteen American service members have been killed in the war. Trump knew this months prior, did nothing to protect service members.

“Farmers, ranchers, and businesses of all kinds are suffering greatly from this.”

Trump lied.

Ukrainian strikes forced Russia to ban diesel exports, which tightened global supply, but the main cause of record US diesel prices is the war with Iran. Tehran closed the Strait of Hormuz after the first US and Israeli strikes in February, and shipping crude out of the Gulf now costs about $33 a barrel, up from about $2. NBC reported that Trump has tried to blame the Ukraine conflict for record diesel prices rather than his own war on Iran.

“Russia is, nevertheless, sending, at a low price, millions of barrels of diesel to the World.”

Trump lied.

Russia isn’t sending diesel out of goodwill. It is selling it under a deal Trump negotiated with Putin, after the Treasury licensed transactions in Russian diesel, including US imports, through April 2027. Russian industry experts had already been calling for the export ban to be lifted because Russia was losing profit. The shipments come to about ten days of US consumption and are expected to do little for prices. Trump provides nothing to back up “at a low price.”

May 5, 1945. A minister and his pregnant wife take five kids from their Sunday school on a picnic in the woods near Bly, Oregon.

Within minutes, six of them are dead.

They were killed by a weapon launched from Japan, more than 5,000 miles away.

Most Americans have never heard of it.

By late 1944 Japan was losing badly. It wanted a way to hit the American mainland, and it came up with one of the strangest weapons of the war.

Balloons.

Huge ones, more than 30 feet across, made from thin paper glued together in layers. A lot of that work was done by Japanese schoolgirls. The balloons were filled with hydrogen and loaded with bombs and incendiaries.

Then they were released into the jet stream.

Riding winds high over the Pacific, they could cross to North America in about three days. A clever system of sandbags and altitude sensors kept them at the right height. When the ballast ran out, the bombs dropped.

The goal was to start massive forest fires and spread panic.
